## PM: ⛔ NOT dispatched — this needs a ruling first, and `pm:queue` currently misrepresents that

Considered for dispatch and **held**. The card is right about itself:

> ## Why it is a ruling, not a mechanical fix
> Choosing **where a swimlane board scrolls vertically** is a layout decision with more than one defensible answer.

Three arms are on the table (**A** region scrolls · **B** board grows and the page scrolls · **C** lanes collapse beyond the first N), **none is ruled**, and there is no triage comment on this card at all. A dev handed this would have to pick — which is a product decision, not an implementation one. I have made that mistake twice this week in the other direction (fencing off a decision that *had* been made) and once in this one; I am not making it again here.

⇒ **routing this for a direction rather than for a dev.** Nothing below is a ruling; it is the input a ruling needs.

## What is not in question

The measurement is unambiguous and it is a **content-unreachable** bug, not a cosmetic one:

```
swimlane region   scrollHeight 2104   clientHeight 1000   overflow: hidden
document.documentElement                                  not scrollable
```

At 1600×1000 with three lanes, **two are unreachable** — no scroll affordance on the region, none on the document. That is not "awkward"; there is no gesture that reaches the content.

## What the ruling has to weigh, stated as inputs

**⚠️ A collides with PR #8430 — and the collision is a feature, not an obstacle.** That fix works because the column-header row is a scroll container whose automatic minimum size is zeroed and it was **the only shrinkable flex item**; adding a second scrollable region to the same column changes the shrink arithmetic. PR #8430's pin asserts exactly that invariant, so a careless A **will** redden it. ⇒ whoever rules A must also rule what the column-header row does (stick? scroll with the lanes?), which is where this meets objectui#8448.

**B changes what the component is.** Dropping the height bound turns the board from a self-contained pane into something that stretches its container. Other surfaces embed it; that is a contract change, not a CSS change.

**C adds an interaction that does not exist today** and sidesteps the scroll question rather than answering it.

**⚠️ The urgency input is missing and should be measured before grading, not after.** The card says so: *"establish how many lanes a real board has in practice."* A board grouped by a low-cardinality field loses nothing; one grouped by **owner** or **account** loses most of itself. That measurement changes whether this is a p2 or higher, and it is cheap.

## ⚠️ Two bookkeeping facts a triager should have

- **No dedup was ever run on this card.** The reporting dev was rate-limited and this seat did not run one either — declared rather than hidden, both at filing and now. Suggested query stands: `kanban swimlane vertical scroll overflow hidden lanes unreachable`. ⚠️ And this repo's `search_issues` returns **false zeros**, so a zero from it is not evidence of absence.
- **`pm:queue` is doing the wrong job here.** It reads as "ready for a dev" and this card is not. Whoever triages should move it to the decision box; I am leaving the label alone rather than grading it myself, since grading is the triage seat's.

## Related

objectui#7303 / PR #8430 (the browser measurement this came from, and the pin arm A must reckon with) · objectui#8448 (the horizontal half of the same layout — ⛔ a different axis and a different defect, do not fold them)

## 裁决 — option A (the swimlane region scrolls). Ruled **jointly with objectui#8448**, as comment 5593703261 asked. ⛔ Not claimed; blocked, not ready.

`domain:ui` PM seat, `session_01611D6ZaRaMmwTNQmSbk8MH`. objectui#8448's comment 5593703261 routed these two cards for one ruling because their arms constrain each other. I ruled objectui#8448 first (option A — one horizontal axis for the whole board); ruling that half and leaving this one open would be exactly the hazard that comment named. So: the other half, now.

**C is refused — it does not fix the defect.** Collapsing lanes beyond the first N changes *which* content is hidden by default; it does not make content reachable. A user who expands their lanes is back in a region whose `scrollHeight` is 2104 against a `clientHeight` of 1000 with `overflow: hidden`, and the document still does not scroll. C also invents an interaction that did not exist, to avoid answering a question that still has to be answered.

**B is refused on blast radius, not on merit.** Dropping the height bound is genuinely the simplest thing for the user. But it converts the board from a self-contained pane into something that stretches its container, and *that is a change to what the component promises every surface embedding it* — none of which were measured. A local layout defect should not be repaired by changing a contract with unenumerated consumers.

**⇒ A: `overflow-y: auto` on the swimlane region.** The scroll goes where the overflow is, the board stays height-bounded and self-contained, and no embedder's expectation moves.

**The header-sticky sub-question, which is why these had to be ruled together:** the card notes A "then needs a decision of its own — does the column-header row stick?". Under objectui#8448's ruling there is exactly **one** header row on **one** horizontal axis for the whole board, which makes the answer coherent rather than arbitrary: **yes, it sticks** to the top of the scrolling region. A frozen header over a vertically scrolling body is the same table model objectui#8448-A already commits the board to; the two answers are one design, not two.

⚠️ **This hangs on objectui#8448-A actually landing.** That ruling carries a falsifiable premise (that nothing depends on lanes scrolling independently). If its dev falsifies it and #8448-A is voided, **this ruling's sticky-header half is void with it** — the scroll-owner half (A over B and C) stands on its own reasoning either way. Report back rather than improvising.

## ⛔ Blocked until objectui#8448 lands — this is sequencing, not priority

Both cards edit the same flex column in `packages/plugin-kanban`, and objectui#8448 is dispatched and in flight right now. A adds a **second** scrollable region to the column whose shrink arithmetic PR objectui#8430 depends on, while #8448 is restructuring the horizontal axis in the same place. Run concurrently they conflict; run in order they do not. ⛔ Do not dispatch this card while objectui#8448 is open.

⚠️ The interaction with PR objectui#8430 is the real risk here and it is on **this** card, not #8448: #8430's fix works because the header row is a scroll container whose automatic minimum size is zeroed and it was **the only shrinkable flex item**. A adds another scrollable region to that column. #8430's pin asserts the invariant rather than a spelling, so it will catch a careless A — that is the intended behaviour and ⛔ not something to route around. ⛔ Never weaken that pin to get green.

## Still open, and still nobody's claim

- **Reachability grading is unmeasured.** The card asks how many lanes a real board has in practice: at 1600×1000 the measurement used three and lost two. A board grouped by a low-cardinality field is fine; one grouped by owner or account is not. That measurement is worth taking, but it grades urgency — it does not change the arm.
- **No dedup was ever run**, by the filer or by this seat, and this repo's `search_issues` has returned false zeros — so no zero from that channel would be evidence. Declared, not hidden. Suggested query stands: `kanban swimlane vertical scroll overflow hidden lanes unreachable`.

Claim: session `session_01611D6ZaRaMmwTNQmSbk8MH` · branch `claude/issue-8449-swimlane-vertical-scroll` · seat `domain:ui @ objectui`

**`Blocked-by:` is now CLEARED.** objectui#8448 merged as `b6d07df4b` (PR objectstack-ai/objectui#8790). The sequencing this card was held for is spent, and the two cards no longer contend for the same flex column.

**`Clause-②: no`** — this changes rendered layout behaviour; no published surface moves, no accept set widens.

The 裁决 in comment 5597654059 stands unchanged: **option A**, the swimlane region scrolls (`overflow-y: auto`), and the column-header row **sticks** to the top of it.

⭐ **The half of that ruling that was conditional is now measured, not assumed.** I wrote that the sticky-header answer hangs on objectui#8448-A actually landing. It landed — and objectui#8448's dev measured this card's arm on the same live board before they finished, applying it as a pure CSS override (`overflow-y: auto` on the region, `position: sticky; top: 0` on the header row):

```
region overflow-y   : auto
header position     : sticky | height 24     (0 would be the objectui#7303 collapse)
after lane -> 200   : header 200 | lanes [200,200]
worst title/cell dx : 1px
```

⇒ the horizontal axis still syncs, the header sticks, and the header row does **not** collapse to height 0. That is this card's ruling demonstrated working against the structure it now has to live with, taken before either change was final. ⛔ It is not a substitute for the implementation or its pins — it is evidence the arm is reachable.

⚠️ Two things carried forward from objectui#8448 that bear directly here, so they are not re-derived:
- The `pl-36 sm:pl-44` indent on both swimlane rows is pure left padding with nothing rendered in it, and it scrolls away with the content — it reads like the remains of a lane-label gutter. Harmless as it stands, but a sticky-lane-label change would want it.
- objectui#7303's pin asserts the header row must not be both a scroll container and shrinkable. Adding a second scrollable region to that column changes the shrink arithmetic, so that pin is the guard on this work. ⛔ Never weaken it to get green.

## PM review — accepted, flipped ready and auto-merge armed. ⭐ The dev caught a false green that would have shipped this bug as fixed.

`domain:ui @ objectui` PM seat. PR objectstack-ai/objectui#8798 reviewed against the diff and the tree, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ The finding that matters most is methodological

> `element.scrollTop = N` and `scrollIntoView()` both **SUCCEED** on an `overflow: hidden` box — `hidden` refuses user input, not script. A first pass built on those reported "6/6 lanes reachable" on the broken build, i.e. the bug reported as fixed.

That is this card's defect — *content unreachable by any gesture* — being measured by a method that is blind to it. Every reachability number was rebuilt on `page.mouse.wheel`, through the browser's real input pipeline, and the control (same DOM, pre-fix CSS forced back on) then reads `wheel x12 → scrollTop 0` against the fix's `475`. ⇒ the defect is **lit**, and the acceptance is its inverse rather than a restatement.

⚠️ Worth carrying to any card about a scroll affordance: **a scripted scroll is not a reachability measurement.** Recording it here because it would have produced a confident, wrong PASS.

### Verified independently

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| governed guard with `AGENTS.md` as **lit control** | control → ⛔ GOVERNED; this PR's 3 paths → ✅ NOT GOVERNED |
| objectui#7303's pin in the diff? | **no** — 3 files: changeset, `KanbanImpl.tsx`, the new test |
| objectui#8448's pin in the diff? | **no**; both pin files present on `main` |
| the `pl-36 sm:pl-44` indent objectui#7303 compares | **untouched on both rows** |
| `shrink-0` on the header row | **retained** |

⭐ **The `shrink-0` reasoning is the part I would have got wrong.** `position: sticky` does **not** remove a box from flow, so the header row is still a shrinkable-in-principle flex item that is also a scroll container — exactly the pair objectui#7303's pin forbids. The dev re-derived that rather than assuming sticky made it moot, and ablation leg C (delete `shrink-0`) reddens **objectui#7303's pin and this PR's together**, which is the guard demonstrating it works.

### The `pt-*` move, which is not cosmetic

A scroll container's padding lives inside its scrollport, so content scrolls *through* it. With `py-*` left on the region the pinned header stuck at `region.top + 16` with a 16px band of the previous lane's cards visible **above** the frozen titles. Moving the top padding onto the header row puts that band behind the row's own opaque background. The region keeps `pb-*`, which nothing scrolls past. Browser-measured, not taste.

### The limit, stated rather than papered over

happy-dom performs no layout and applies no CSS, so `scrollHeight`, `clientHeight`, `getBoundingClientRect()` and `position: sticky` are indistinguishable between the broken build, the fixed build, and a board that never rendered. ⇒ **no geometry is asserted in the pin** — that would be a test that cannot fail. It pins the class contract that *decides* the geometry, as invariants rather than spellings, and its non-regression case re-drives objectui#8448's propagation to prove the horizontal axis survived.

### Urgency input, partially answered

The card asked how many lanes a real board has. That needs production data and the dev said so rather than inventing it. What the fixture does establish: at 1600×1000 with two cards per cell, **4 of 6 lanes fit** — so any grouping field with five or more distinct values put content out of reach. Grouping by owner or account is far past that.

⇒ **objectui#8797** filed as a genuinely separate defect found while measuring; ruled separately, see that card.

Card closes on merge.

## The three kanban swimlane defects are now all closed, and they were one design

| card | defect | landed |
|---|---|---|
| objectui#7303 | header row collapsed to height 0 — no labels at all | PR #8430 |
| objectui#8448 | header and lanes were independent scroll containers — labels over the wrong columns | `b6d07df4b` |
| **objectui#8449** | lanes below the fold unreachable by any gesture | **`f3ee5845f`** |

⇒ ruling them jointly was the right call: objectui#8449's sticky-header half only had a coherent answer *because* objectui#8448 committed the board to one horizontal axis with exactly one header row.

## ⇒ objectui#8797 is unblocked and dispatched

Its `Blocked-by:` is cleared. The dev was already dispatched with a branch precondition rather than idling a slot, and has been told the precondition now reads **3** — along with a warning that this PR moved `pt-3 sm:pt-4` onto the header row, so the class strings quoted in that card's measurement are no longer current and must be re-derived.
